title: Catalog provenance badges and copy scraps
body:
Goal: quick brainstorm + rough wire notes for adding provenance/trust badges to model cards, and refining copy for endpoint creation + pin/fallback flows. Aim to reduce accidental pinning, increase trust signals, and make fallback behavior explicit in the endpoint wizard.

Context/why:
- PMs and SRE reported customers confused when a pinned version falls back to a quantized/compat model (support tickets: ENG-2417).
- Sales asked for clearer signals about model lineage (origin, tested benchmarks, certs) on listing cards for enterprise audits.
- We want to avoid overloading catalog UI; badges should be small, scannable, and tappable for details.

High-level heuristics we want to follow:
- Single-line badges (icon + 2–3 chars) that expand into a short tooltip when hovered/tapped. Keep badges consistent with Console color tokens.
- Primary trust badges only on list cards: "Origin", "Quant", "Verified", "Security-Checked", "Pinned". Secondary meta appears in the detail panel/expanded card.
- Any badge that implies a behavioral difference (e.g., Pinned, Fallback-Allowed) must surface the action consequences in the endpoint creation flow before the user confirms.

Wireframe notes (card + expanded panel):
- Card (compact):
  - Left: model thumbnail (small).
  - Middle: model name + short desc \u2014 below that a single row of 3 badges max (wrap to 2 lines if >3).
  - Right: quick actions (Pin icon toggle, Compare checkbox, Create endpoint CTA).
  - Badge example: [P] Pinned (purple outline) | [V] Verified (green) | [Q] Quant (amber) | [O] Origin (blue)
  - Tooltips on badges: short one-liners (see copy below).

- Expanded details (drawer):
  - Top: model header + big provenance block (breadcrumb of origin: repo -> packaging run -> derived-from). Each breadcrumb is clickable to audit logs.
  - Middle: measurable signals: latency bench, perf SLO, quantization compatibility note, recommended endpoint profile.
  - Bottom: actions: Pin version, Create endpoint (quick), Add to Workspace.

Copy micro-variants (tooltips and CTAs). We should A/B test short vs. explicit copy.
- Badge tooltip: Pinned (short) variant A: "Pinned: fixed to this version for predictable outputs." Variant B: "Pinned: endpoints using this pin will not auto-upgrade; rollouts require manual change or can be configured with canary rules."
- Badge tooltip: Quant (short) A: "Quantized: smaller model size, lower memory; slight accuracy tradeoffs possible." B: "Quantized: optimized for throughput. See bench results in details."
- Badge tooltip: Verified A: "Verified by Redwood: smoke-tested on core benchmarks." B: "Redwood-verified: passed regression and safety checks for general-purpose prompts."

Endpoint creation copy flow (quick-create modal + confirm):
- Quick-create first screen: name + route. Beneath route, inline note when model is pinned or has fallback config: e.g., "Using model v1.3 (pinned). If capacity constrained, requests may fallback to v1.3-quant. Configure fallback rules in advanced settings."
- Advanced settings accordion: Fallback policy (radio): 
  - PreferPinned: Always prefer pinned; queue until pinned capacity available (default for enterprise).
  - FallbackToCompatible: Allow fallback to compatible quantized variants when latency or capacity constraints occur.
  - RegionalFallback: Route to another region's compatible variant if primary is unhealthy.
- Confirm CTA states: "Create endpoint (1 region)". If fallback enabled show link: "View fallback chain" (opens small side panel with chain visualization).

Copy drafts for confirm modal when pin+fallback mixed (friction area):
- Option 1 (explicit): "This endpoint will pin to Model X v1.3. If capacity is limited, Redwood may route some requests to compatible variants (e.g., v1.3-quant). Expected differences: up to 2% generation quality variance. You can disable fallbacks in Advanced Settings."
- Option 2 (concise): "Pinned to v1.3. Fallbacks allowed to compatible variants. Disable in Advanced."
- Option 3 (tooling-friendly): "Pinned to v1.3 — View fallback chain (details) | Edit policy"

Questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Should badges be searchable/filterable? (idea: filter by Verified/Quant/Origin). Search priority: customers asked for Verified filter. Quick win but adds UI complexity in list controls.
- What is the canonical short form for Origin? "O" vs "Src" vs server icon. Need design preference.
- Should the "Pinned" badge be interactive on the card (toggle) or require the details drawer? Toggle is fast but invites accidental pin/unpin. Maybe require confirmation on toggle.

Backlog grooming (proposed tickets + rough sizing):
- UX-889 Add provenance badges to catalog cards + tooltips (2 wks) -> wireframes, tokens, copy variants, A11y checks.
- ENG-2417 Endpoint wizard: surface fallback policy and pin consequences (3 wks) -> backend: ensure endpoint create API returns (pinned, fallbackOptions) flags.
- UX-898 Filter chips for Verified/Quant/Origin on catalog (1 wk) -> MVP: add search chip + server-side indexing.
- DEV-PR-564 small: add audit-links to expanded model panel (3 days).

Microcopy checklist for engineers (what to implement first):
- Short tooltip texts (<= 80 chars) for badges.
- Confirm modal copy (Option 1 explicit) as default for enterprise orgs; Option 2 for orgs below threshold.
- Show small fallback icon next to route name in endpoint list if fallback allowed.
- Emit telemetry event when user toggles pin and when they change fallback policy (for later UX analysis).

A/B test ideas:
- Tooltip length: short vs. explicit (measure time-to-pin, support tickets).
- Pin toggle location: card toggle vs. details-only (measure accidental toggles and help center clicks).
- Fallback wording: numeric variance (e.g., "may change outputs" vs. "expected up to 2% variance") to see if concrete numbers reduce tickets.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Run a 1-hour design pairing with Liam to lock down badge iconography.
- Collect enterprise feedback from Mateo on compliance wording for "Origin" provenance.
- Add clarifying sentence to docs: how to interpret "Verified" vs. "Security-Checked" (these are different internal checks).
- Prepare a short demo flow for the next PM sync showing the confirm modal with explicit fallback chain.

Slack threads / refs: #catalog-redesign (pinning convo), #sre-feedback (fall back incidents).

Random copy snippets we might like to stash: (use as microcopy playground)
- "Pinned to keep outputs stable. Rollouts require a manual change or scheduled canaries."
- "Fallbacks are an availability safeguard: they prioritize request success over exact parity."
- "Verified by Redwood: smoke-tested on small set of public prompts. Not a guarantee for all downstream tasks."

End of notes.

(Change log)
- 2024-10-18 Samira: initial brain dump and wireframe notes.
- 2024-10-25 Liam: added A/B ideas and sketch clarifications.
- 2024-11-03 Priya: clarified endpoint confirm language and added jira refs.
